question.text: Let $\alpha, \beta$ be the roots of $x^{2}-x-1=0$ and $S_{n}=\alpha^{n}+\beta^{n},$ for all integers $n \geq 1 .$ Then, for every integer $n \geq 2$

solution.text:
Given, $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of $x^{2}-x-1=0$
$\therefore \quad \alpha+\beta=1$
and $\alpha \beta=-1$
Now, consider option (a). $S_{n}+S_{n-1}=S_{n+1}$
Put $n=2$, we get, $\quad S_{2}+S_{1}=S_{3}$ $\therefore \quad\left(\alpha^{2}+\beta^{2}\right)+(\alpha+\beta)=\alpha^{3}+\beta^{3}$
$\left[\because \cdot S_{n}=\alpha^{n}+\beta^{n},\right.$ given]
$\Rightarrow(a+\beta)^{2}-2 a \beta+(\alpha+\beta)$
$=(\alpha+\beta)^{3}-3 \alpha \beta(\alpha+\beta)$
$\Rightarrow 1^{2}-2(-1)+1=1^{3}-3(-1)(1)$
$\Rightarrow 2+1=1+3$
$\Rightarrow \quad 1+2+1=1+3$
$\Rightarrow$
$4=4,$ which is true.
Hence, option (a) is correct.
